To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new analytical technique of L 1 scheme is introduced to analyze a new class of time fractional mixed subdiffusion and diffusion wave equations, and that the stability and convergence of this scheme are proved rigorou

we have developed new analytical tools to analyze the standard difference schemes for multi term fractional differential equations and the new analytical technique has been successfully applied to analyze a multi term time fractional mixed sub-diffusion and diffusion wave equation.

a new analytical technique of L type difference schemes is introduced to analyze time fractional mixed subdiffusion and diffusion wave equations and a new analytical technique is used to analyze time fractional diffusion equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical approximation of a time fractional mixed subdiffusion and diffusion-wave equation.
the following time fractional mixed sub-diffusion and diffusion-wave equations involving at least two time fractional derivatives of order g and a respectively.
the analysis of a new numerical method based on the L 1 scheme for a class of mixed time fractional differential problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L 1 type schemes can be used to solve multi term mixed time derivatives of any order and any number of terms.
the proposed analytical technique is very useful in analyzing the standard finite difference scheme based on L type scheme.
the L 1 scheme is unconditionally stable and convergent in the discrete H 1 sense with the temporal convergence of the optimal order O t min 1 2 a 2 g.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established the first rigorous analysis for the L type finite difference scheme of the mixed sub diffusion and wave equation.
the L 1 type scheme is stable and convergent for a wide range of mixed fractional order derivatives.
a novel analytical technique is developed to analyze the L type difference scheme for the time fractional mixed subdiffusion and diffusion wave equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L type difference scheme for the multi term mixed time derivative equations can achieve the optimal temporal accuracy in a discrete H k norm for k 1 2.
we provide a general framework for analyzing multi term fractional differential equations.
the stability analysis of the difference scheme is based on the energy estimate of the exact solution and the stability analysis is independent of the numerical solution of the difference scheme.
